summary: Wire MiddlewareRegistry.load_plugins() into both Python server bootstraps so out-of-tree plugins discovered through Python entry-points (group sox_protocol.plugins) compose with the default pipeline. The existing core/middleware/registry.py already exposes a permissive load_entry_points(group='sox_protocol.middleware') that registers any zero-arg callable; that path remains for legacy in-tree middleware. P4 layers a manifest-validating loader on top: a new core/middleware/plugin_loader.py reads sox-plugin.yaml from each discovered package, validates against spec/schemas/sox-plugin.schema.json, runs the §4 boot-time protocol_version compatibility check (PEP 440 + npm caret dual-form per 06-versioning.md), enforces capability-flag orthogonality, runs a stable Kahn topological sort with lex-id tie-break, and instantiates plugin factories via the entry_point.load() handle. The seven closed-taxonomy error envelopes from 03-plugin-contract.md §6.2 (plugin_not_allowed, plugin_not_found, plugin_manifest_invalid, plugin_protocol_version_mismatch, plugin_capability_conflict, plugin_ordering_cycle, plugin_requirement_unmet) are emitted as structured errors during this load; all are fail-fast at startup.
summary_part2: MiddlewareRegistry gains a single new public method: load_plugins(*, allowlist: list[str] | None = None, env: str = 'dev', host_protocol_version: str = '1.0.0', no_discovery: bool = False) -> None. It orchestrates: (1) entry-point scan; (2) per-plugin manifest read + JSON-Schema validate; (3) protocol_version negotiation; (4) capability-flag orthogonality assertion; (5) allowlist filter (production-empty=refuse-all; dev-warn-on-unallowlisted); (6) toposort with cycle detection; (7) requires/provides resolution; (8) factory invocation + register(). Result is cached on the registry as the resolved order property — Kahn runs once at startup, never per-request. Both bootstraps (core/mcp_server/server.py lifespan; adapters/transports/http/server.py create_app) call registry.load_plugins() AFTER build_default_pipeline; the new plugins extend rather than replace the default chain. CLI (cli/serve.py) gains --allow-plugins ID,... and --no-discovery flags; SOX_ALLOWED_PLUGINS and SOX_ENV env vars provide the equivalent declarative path with --allow-plugins taking precedence per 03-plugin-contract.md §6.1.
summary_part3: P4 deliberately does NOT redesign any contract: it implements the contract frozen by B1. Per ADR 0004 §6 the v1 host validates that signatures is present and is a list but does not enforce contents. Per 06-versioning.md §6.2 the host emits a non-zero exit and the five-field plugin_protocol_version_mismatch envelope on incompatibility. Per analysis §7.5 risk #1 production mode (SOX_ENV=production) with empty allowlist refuses to load any plugin — this is fail-fast supply-chain protection, not silent degradation. --no-discovery short-circuits the entire loader before allowlist evaluation (precedence rule documented in R4) so security audits and unit tests can run hermetically without site-packages contamination.

Add read_manifest_for_entry_point(ep): import the entry-point's distribution (importlib.metadata.distribution(ep.dist.name)); locate sox-plugin.yaml via the package's [project.entry-points.'sox_protocol.plugins'] convention (declared next to the entry-point package's __init__ — fall back to walking distribution.files for sox-plugin.yaml). Add validate_manifest(doc): jsonschema.validate against spec/schemas/sox-plugin.schema.json; on failure raise PluginManifestInvalid with the validator's path + message. Validate that signatures is present and is a list (per ADR 0004 §6, do not enforce contents).

Add check_protocol_version(manifest, host_protocol_version): apply the §4.2 algorithm (parse → test → reject). Use prereleases=True when host version contains a pre-release identifier per 06-versioning.md §4.4. On mismatch raise PluginProtocolVersionMismatch carrying the five-field envelope from §5.1.

Add assert_capability_orthogonality(manifest): scan plugin_capabilities for the {observe_only:true} + {may_short_circuit:true} pair; on conflict raise PluginCapabilityConflict per 03-plugin-contract.md §2.3.

Add canonicalize_env_var(plugin_id, key) -> str helper implementing the §7.2 rule (replace . and - with _; uppercase; SOX_PLUGIN_<id>_<KEY>). Used by future config readers; included here as the loader is the natural home.

files.purpose: Add the seven closed-taxonomy plugin startup error classes per 03-plugin-contract.md §6.2.
files.target_state: Adds PluginStartupError(MiddlewareError) base + seven typed subclasses each carrying error_code as a stable class-level constant.
delta: Add class PluginStartupError(MiddlewareError) base with error_code: ClassVar[str] and to_envelope() -> dict[str, str] method.
Add PluginNotAllowed(PluginStartupError, error_code='plugin_not_allowed') — config typo / unallowlisted id; envelope echoes the offending id.
Add PluginNotFound(PluginStartupError, error_code='plugin_not_found') — allowlist entry references no entry-point.
Add PluginManifestInvalid(PluginStartupError, error_code='plugin_manifest_invalid') — schema validation failed; carries jsonschema path.
Add PluginProtocolVersionMismatch(PluginStartupError, error_code='plugin_protocol_version_mismatch') — five-field envelope: plugin_id, plugin_declares, host_supports, remediation.
Add PluginCapabilityConflict(PluginStartupError, error_code='plugin_capability_conflict') — observe_only+may_short_circuit set together.
Add PluginOrderingCycle(PluginStartupError, error_code='plugin_ordering_cycle') — message MUST name cycle members in arrow notation.
Add PluginRequirementUnmet(PluginStartupError, error_code='plugin_requirement_unmet') — names unmet capability + requiring plugin id.

files.purpose: Add load_plugins() orchestrator on MiddlewareRegistry; re-export the resolved order as a cached property.
files.current_state: Has load_entry_points(group='sox_protocol.middleware') (lines 177-200) — naive loader, no manifest/allowlist/version checks, called by no production code.
files.target_state: Adds load_plugins(*, allowlist, env, host_protocol_version, no_discovery, group='sox_protocol.plugins') method that performs the seven-step pipeline (scan→manifest-validate→version-negotiate→orthogonality→allowlist→toposort→register). Caches resolved order on self._resolved_order. Existing load_entry_points kept untouched for backward compat with in-tree middleware that still register that way.
delta: Import from sox_protocol.core.middleware.plugin_loader: read_manifest_for_entry_point, validate_manifest, check_protocol_version, assert_capability_orthogonality.
Import error classes from sox_protocol.core.middleware.errors.
Add self._loaded_manifests: dict[str, Manifest] = {} and self._resolved_order: tuple[str, ...] | None = None on __init__.
Add load_plugins(*, allowlist: list[str] | None = None, env: str = 'dev', host_protocol_version: str = '1.0.0', no_discovery: bool = False, group: str = 'sox_protocol.plugins') -> None.
Step 0: if no_discovery: log INFO 'plugin discovery disabled (--no-discovery)'; set self._resolved_order = (); return.
Step 1: enumerate importlib.metadata.entry_points(group=group); collect (ep.name, ep) tuples.
Step 2: in production mode (env=='production') with empty/None allowlist: log+raise PluginNotAllowed (allowlist_required) — refuses startup; non-empty allowlist proceeds.

Step 3: for each entry-point: read_manifest_for_entry_point(ep) → validate_manifest → check_protocol_version → assert_capability_orthogonality. Each raise propagates as the right typed error and aborts startup.

Step 4: allowlist filter — for each manifest.id: if env=='production' and id not in allowlist: skip silently per 03-plugin-contract.md §6.1; if env=='dev' and allowlist provided and id not in allowlist: emit stderr warning + load anyway. For each id IN allowlist that produced no manifest: raise PluginNotFound(id).

Step 5: build DAG over loaded manifests using must_run_before/must_run_after; resolve capability strings via the {provides → set[plugin_id]} index built from each manifest.plugin_capabilities. Run stable Kahn (existing _topological_sort generalized; add lex tie-break confirmation) and on incompletion raise PluginOrderingCycle naming remaining nodes.
Step 6: validate requires — for each manifest: every entry in requires resolved against the provides index; missing → raise PluginRequirementUnmet(plugin=id, capability=req).
Step 7: invoke factories — for each ordered id call ep.load()() and self.register(id, factory). Cache self._resolved_order = tuple(ordered_ids).
Step 8: log structured 'plugin registry frozen: N plugins loaded' line per ADR §9.1.
Add @property resolved_order(self) -> tuple[str, ...] returning self._resolved_order or () if load_plugins not yet called.
Do NOT modify load_entry_points — keep as-is for backward compatibility.

risks.title: PEP 440 ~= vs npm ~ semantic mismatch
risks.detail: PEP 440 ~=1.0 means >=1.0,<2 (compatible-release); npm ~1.0 means >=1.0.0,<1.1.0 (patch-only). A naive single-parser implementation will silently swap semantics depending on which parser sees the string first.
risks.mitigation: parse_version_range() in plugin_loader.py MUST attempt PEP 440 first (canonical per 06-versioning.md §2.2), and only fall back to npm-form normalization when the input contains a leading caret/tilde-with-no-spec or wildcard 'x'. Add a unit test covering '~=1.0' (PEP 440 → matches 1.5) vs '~1.0.0' (npm → does NOT match 1.5) on the same host version to lock the disambiguation.

risks.title: Tests need a stub plugin without polluting site-packages
risks.detail: Integration tests must inject an entry-point so importlib.metadata.entry_points(group='sox_protocol.plugins') yields it, but pip install -e into the dev venv is unacceptable for hermetic CI.
risks.mitigation: Use monkeypatch on importlib.metadata.entry_points to return a synthetic EntryPoint whose .load() returns a fixture factory and whose .dist points at a tmp_path with a stub METADATA + sox-plugin.yaml. Fallback: write a real .dist-info into a tmp_path and prepend to sys.path via monkeypatch — fewer mocks, more realism — choose this if the EntryPoint constructor proves brittle across importlib.metadata versions.

risks.title: --allow-plugins vs --no-discovery interaction
risks.detail: If both --no-discovery and --allow-plugins=foo,bar are passed, do we allow startup with a stale allowlist that references nothing? Spec is silent.
risks.mitigation: Decision: --no-discovery short-circuits the loader entirely BEFORE allowlist evaluation. Allowlist contents are not validated, no PluginNotFound is raised, resolved_order = (). Document this precedence in load_plugins() docstring AND in cli/serve.py --no-discovery help text. Test test_no_discovery_short_circuits asserts this.
risks.spec_ref: ADR 0004 decision 4 (allowlist) — spec silent on interaction; project decision recorded here.

risks.title: signatures field reservation enforcement scope
risks.detail: v1 hosts MUST validate that signatures is present and is a list, but MUST NOT enforce contents (06-versioning.md §6.2). Easy to over-implement.
risks.mitigation: validate_manifest() asserts presence + list type only; non-empty arrays log a one-time INFO 'signature verification deferred to v1.x'. Test test_signatures_present_but_contents_unenforced asserts a manifest with arbitrary signature items still loads cleanly.

risks.title: load_entry_points() legacy path coexistence
risks.detail: Existing core/middleware/registry.py:load_entry_points uses group='sox_protocol.middleware' (singular), differs from new group='sox_protocol.plugins'. Two parallel discovery paths could cause name collisions.
risks.mitigation: load_plugins() uses the NEW group exclusively; load_entry_points() left untouched but its docstring updated to note it is legacy / deprecated for v1.x removal. If a name collision is detected during register(), MiddlewareRegistry.register raises ValueError today — that surfaces as PluginStartupError inside load_plugins via try/except wrap.

risks.title: Pipeline rebuild vs append strategy not specified by core
risks.detail: Both bootstraps need to fold loaded plugins into the already-constructed Pipeline returned by build_default_pipeline. Pipeline today is built via PipelineBuilder; mid-flight extension API isn't documented in core/middleware/__init__.py.
risks.mitigation: Phase 02-build's plugin_loader.py and registry.py changes do NOT modify Pipeline. The bootstrap-integration phase (04) chooses ONE strategy: rebuild via PipelineBuilder seeded with default_chain components plus registered plugin factories. A small helper extend_pipeline_with_registry(p: Pipeline, r: MiddlewareRegistry) -> Pipeline can live in core/middleware/default_chain.py if needed; this is a minor extension, not a contract change. Spec compliance: cached order rule (4.1) is preserved because the pipeline is rebuilt once at startup, never per-request.
